shortcut_name: binary-positive dot products reduce the task to triangle finding
evidence: gpt-oss-120b uses "bitset of neighbors" and checks "edge i-j exists"; glm-5 builds "adj = [set()...]" and searches for neighbors that are "connected"
affordance_in_statement: Upon receiving this pulse, registry u sets the k-th element of its vector to 1 (V_u[k] = 1), and registry v sets the k-th element of its vector to 1 (V_v[k] = 1). ... Let V_a · V_b denote the standard dot product ... A critical resonance anomaly occurs if ... (V_x1 · V_x2) · (V_x1 · V_x3) · (V_x2 · V_x3) > 0
removal_suggestion: Replace the binary update with a signed pulse-dependent update, so the k-th coordinate is set to a specified signed value rather than always 1. For example, use +1 for k <= 3 and (-1)^k for k > 3, preserving the examples while making dot products depend on signed accumulation rather than mere pair existence.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats every pair with a positive dot product as an ordinary graph edge and searches for the lexicographically first triangle using bitsets.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Every pulse writes 1 to the same coordinate of both endpoint vectors, so a pair has positive dot product exactly when the pair occurs in a pulse.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Stores endpoint pairs as an undirected adjacency set and searches for a connected triple instead of computing vector dot products.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The 0/1 vector updates make positive pairwise dot product equivalent to pair adjacency.

common_affordance: Because all vector entries are nonnegative binary indicators, each positive dot product is equivalent to the existence of at least one pulse joining the two registries, turning the condition into an ordinary graph triangle.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Constructs huge Python integers with one bit per pulse for every registry, causing excessive memory or runtime use at the stated limits.
Explicitly constructs n vectors of length m and then computes pairwise data, leading to prohibitive memory usage and time complexity.

recommended_edit: Change the update rule from setting each endpoint's coordinate to 1 to setting it to a signed pulse-dependent value, retaining +1 for the first three pulses so both examples remain valid. This prevents positive dot products from being represented by simple graph adjacency and invalidates both surviving triangle-only solutions.
